title: The New Student
text:
Last September a new student came to our [[class]]. His name was Kevin, and he had just moved here from another [[city]]. On his first morning he stood at the [[door]] of the classroom and did not say a word. Our [[teacher]] asked him to sit next to me.

Kevin was very [[quiet]]. During the first week he only opened his mouth to answer questions. At lunch he ate alone. I wanted to talk to him, but I did not know how to [[begin]].

Then something happened. In art class I forgot my [[eraser]] and could not fix a line I had drawn wrong. Kevin pushed his across the desk without saying anything. I said thank you, and he gave me a small [[smile]].

After that we started to [[talk]]. I learned that he loved to [[draw]]. His [[notebook]] was full of pictures of animals and old buildings. They were much better than anything I could do. I asked him why he never showed them to anyone. He said he was [[afraid]] people would laugh.

The next week our teacher asked the class to make a poster about the [[library]]. I asked Kevin to work with me. He drew, and I wrote the words. When we showed it to the class, everyone said it was [[excellent]]. Kevin's face turned red, but this time he looked pleased.

Now Kevin is not quiet at all. He has many [[friend]]s and he laughs more than I do. Sometimes the person who says nothing is only waiting for someone to ask.

title: A Rainy Day at Home
text:
It rained all weekend, so we had to stay [[home]]. My little sister was bored by ten o'clock in the morning. She walked around the [[living room]] and asked me the same question ten times: "What can we do?"

Father was reading beside the [[window]]. "Why don't you clean your room?" he said. That was not the answer she wanted.

In the end Mother had an [[idea]]. She took an old [[basket]] down from a high shelf and opened it on the [[table]]. Inside were photographs, letters, and a small wooden [[toy]] that had belonged to Grandfather.

We spent the whole [[afternoon]] looking at them. There was a photo of Mother when she was a [[student]], standing in front of her school with two friends. Her hair was long and she wore a white [[uniform]]. My sister could not believe it was the same person.

Then the [[light]] went out. The storm had cut the power. Father found some [[candle]]s in a [[drawer]] and lit three of them. The whole room turned orange and soft.

We could not use the television or the [[computer]], so we talked instead. Father told us about the year he lived in a small house with no hot [[water]]. Mother told us how she and her sister once got lost on a mountain.

The power came back at eight, but nobody turned the television on. Outside the rain was still falling. Inside, for the first time in months, our family sat in one room and simply listened to each other.

title: The Sports Day
text:
Our school holds a [[sport]]s day every November. This year I signed up for the four hundred meter [[race]]. I am not fast, but my friend Leo said I should try.

For three weeks we practiced after school. Every afternoon we ran around the [[playground]] until our legs were [[sore]]. Leo was always ten steps ahead of me. "You are getting better," he said, but I did not believe him.

On the morning of sports day the sky was [[cloudy]] and the air was [[cool]] — good weather for running. Our class wore [[red]] shirts. The other classes wore blue, green, and [[yellow]]. The whole [[school]] looked like a box of crayons.

My race was after lunch. I was so [[afraid]] that I could not eat anything. My [[stomach]] hurt. Leo gave me half of his [[banana]] and told me to breathe slowly.

When the whistle blew, I ran. For the first two hundred meters I was in fourth place. Then a boy in front of me slowed down, and I passed him. I could [[hear]] my classmates shouting my name. My legs felt [[weak]], but I kept going.

I finished third. Not first, not a [[prize]] on the stage, but third out of eight. Leo was waiting at the line and lifted both arms above his head as if he had won.

That evening I could hardly [[walk]] up the stairs. My mother laughed at me. I did not care. Third is not nothing when you started at the back.
